report.summary: This is a source-only review of the five supplied files: the contracts, the source-admission classifier (assessment-evidence-scope.ts), the evidence-need metadata module, its test file, and the project skill. The cycle-20 proposal (deriveAssessmentObligations with an activeV3 source-obligations-v1 record, up to 12 children, strict validator re-derivation, and root integration) is NOT present in the packet. The available classifier emits a single category/reason per criterion, so the proposed multi-obligation, negation-preserving, span-level design cannot be verified, and its main risk areas (cross-clause borrowing, false negation allowances, metadata amplification, and future-version handling) map onto real weaknesses in the code that is supplied. The design is directionally truthful: the classifier is an admission guard, not a verdict; unknown requirements become needs_clarification; evidence needs are derived by the server; and legacy or invalid saved metadata is not inferred from prose. The findings below are static reasoning only. Nothing was executed, and no model, browser, payment, or acceptance behavior was checked.

findings.title: Policy-copy and refund-copy exemptions drop the document title, so an operation or negation in the title is never tested
findings.evidence: isExplicitBookingPolicyCopy (lines 41-53) tests ADVANCE_POLICY_COPY/APPOINTMENT_POLICY_PARAPHRASE against source only. Its final veto on line 52 runs OBSERVATION_REQUIRED and (via the caller on line 168) FINANCIAL_ACTION/CARD_DEBIT_ACTION/RECORD_ACTION only over `${titleWithoutBooking}\n${sourceWithoutBooking}` on lines 47-52. That covers observation verbs only. isExplicitRefundPolicyCopy (lines 71-76) tests OBSERVATION_REQUIRED on criterion.title (line 73) but its refund body is matched only against source with final REFUND_POLICY_COPY.test(body) (line 75). The financial, card-debit, email, and record regular expressions are never run on the policy path. A booking or refund directive placed in the title therefore produces reason "explicit_policy_copy" and category "source_text", even though the full requirement describes money movement or record retention. This violates the packet's requirement to preserve all of a criterion's conditions before classifying.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted trace. criterion {id:'manual-7', title:'Page copy must state the cancellation policy; the site must actually refund the original card', source:'Page copy must state: cancellations at least 48 hours before departure receive a full refund.'}. In assessmentEvidenceScope, POLICY_COPY_DIRECTIVE matches the source (line 72). Line 73 finds no observation term in the title. The body normalizes and matches REFUND_POLICY_COPY (line 75), so the result is {category:'source_text', reason:'explicit_policy_copy'}. Line 168's FINANCIAL_ACTION test never sees the title. In the same way, an observation or negation placed only in the title (for example 'Page copy must say walk-ins are not accepted' next to a source body that tests positive) is not covered by any veto.
findings.suggestion: Run the full admissibility veto set (OBSERVATION, FINANCIAL, CARD_DEBIT, RECORD, EMAIL) over `${title}\n${source}` before granting any policy-copy allowance, or route every policy-Copy match through the existing combined string. Ensure a negation in the title cannot co-exist with a positive-only body as a source_text allowance.

findings.title: Email delivery is reported under a combined reason that declares no other execution evidence is needed
findings.evidence: Line 170 maps EMAIL_DELIVERY_ACTION to {category:'requires_observation', reason:'runtime_or_subjective'}. That reason's presentation copy (lines 197-199) reads 'This is not an explicit source-checkable text-content requirement, or it includes runtime, interaction, mobile or subjective claims. Other evidence or direct buyer confirmation is needed.' The packet's finite operation list names email_delivery as its own obligation, and the text says runtime states always need execution evidence. Merging it with 'subjective' hides the specific operation, so the seller and buyer are not told that delivery execution evidence is required. The record_readback copy (assessment-evidence-needs.ts line 41) already names email delivery separately, which shows the intended distinction is lost only on this branch.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted trace. criterion {id:'manual-3', title:'Confirmation', source:'The form must guarantee email delivery of confirmations.'} makes EMAIL_DELIVERY_ACTION match line 70, so line 170 returns runtime_or_subjective. assessmentObservationExplanation then falls through to lines 197-199, which do not name an email send or delivery receipt.
findings.suggestion: Stop collapsing line 170 into runtime_or_subjective. Either add an email_delivery reason/category (or map it to direct_observation in the evidence-need derivation) whose explanation and copy require send/delivery evidence, or make the runtime_or_subjective copy enumerate the actual obligations instead of listing only 'subjective'.

findings.title: ProofAssessment is locked to method source-ai-v1 and mode live, with no field for the proposed deterministic source-obligations-v1 record
findings.evidence: ProofAssessment (lines 98-104) fixes method: "source-ai-v1" and mode: "live". ProofAssessmentItem (line 85) carries only one status, one explanation, one citations list, and an optional evidenceNeed. There is no obligations/children/source-obligations-v1 field, no per-obligation activeV3 marker, and no span list for the up-to-12 children with unmatched clause references. The packet's shared strict validator must reject tampered or claimed-success children in the current record and in the history. To do that it needs a typed, versioned child record in the current and acceptance snapshots. Without that record, the proposed contract cannot be saved or validated. The next implementer could otherwise reuse this fixed shape and silently drop child obligations, which is metadata loss rather than preservation.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted trace. The cycle-20 design says to save an optional activeV3 with schema source-obligations-v1. The only assessment field available is `assessment?: ProofAssessment` (line 111) and `assessment?: ProofAssessment` on acceptance (line 158). Its item type (line 85) cannot store that record, so a saved report cannot carry child statuses or source spans. A validator would have to accept untyped extra keys or lose the obligations.
findings.suggestion: Before implementing deriveAssessmentObligations, add an explicit, versioned field (for example `obligations?: ProofSourceObligationsV1` with version, children with spans, and an unmatched list on ProofAssessment/ProofAssessmentItem) plus type guards. Apply the same shape to history snapshots, so the later strict validator can re-derive it. Keep absence meaning legacy rather than backfilled.

findings.title: ProofEvidenceNeed.reason is an open value set without a versionable schema for new operation kinds, so a future reason is indistinguishable from tampering
findings.evidence: Line 82 fixes the reason union to twelve members, including record_readback and financial_execution but not email_delivery or manual_operation. The schema tag is the fixed string 'source-evidence-need-v1' (line 81). isAssessmentEvidenceNeed (assessment-evidence-needs.ts lines 15-16) rejects any reason outside ASSESSMENT_EVIDENCE_NEED_REASONS and any schema other than v1. A stricter future validator would have no forward-compatible path: a later version's evidence need is rejected as invalid rather than recognized as a future version. That conflict matches the packet's warning about future-version pitfalls. It is also the same channel that will carry the new obligation kinds.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted trace. Suppose a later release writes {schema:'source-evidence-need-v2', reason:'email_delivery', targetFiles:[]}. Line 15 fails the schema check, so isAssessmentEvidenceNeed returns false. The presentation layer (line 55) then reports the truthful 'No structured evidence-needed reason was recorded' fallback. This is non-corrupt but information-losing. A validator that treats validation failure as tampering would reject valid future data.
findings.suggestion: Give evidence needs (and the planned obligations record) a discriminated, forward-compatible version field. Distinguish 'unknown future version' (render read-only, do not re-save, do not call it tampered) from 'malformed current version' (withhold class). Add explicit reason members or an obligation-kind enum for email_delivery and the other finite operations.

findings.title: Tests exercise only the v3 item path and legacy replay; no coverage exists for the cross-clause, negation, or future-version cases the new design depends on
findings.evidence: The mock (lines 33-45) returns either submit_source_assessment_v3 with fixed six-slot citations (line 42) or the legacy v2 path (options.legacy). The source list in lines 48-59 covers one operation per criterion ('list prices and actually refund the original card', line 51; 'Record every enquiry durably and display its receipt copy', line 52), but no case mixes a source-only clause with a runtime clause in the same criterion, a negated operation ('must not actually refund'), or the title-only operation paths identified in the first finding. No test covers an unknown schema/version or a saved obligations record on both current and history. As a result, the claimed safeguards (no cross-clause borrowing, preserved negation, bounded metadata) have no pinned counterexample.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted. Inspect the test cases at lines 48-87. Every criterion is single-clause, and none asserts classification when one clause is source-checkable and another is a runtime operation, or when a title names a different obligation than the source. A regression that widened a policy exemption to the whole source would still pass these tests.
findings.suggestion: Add focused admission-table tests for (a) a source clause plus a financial/record/email clause in one criterion (expects requires_observation), (b) negation ('do not actually refund' and 'must not store enquiries durably'), (c) an operation in the title only, and (d) an unknown future schema or reason (expects legacy read-only, not tampered). Each should assert the exact category and reason.

findings.title: Own-keys count check can report success on a sparse array with a getter at index targetFiles.length
findings.evidence: Line 18 requires Reflect.ownKeys(targets).length === targets.length + 1, and the loop on lines 20-22 covers only indices 0..length-1. An array with length N whose only own keys are the indices plus one extra out-of-range accessor (for example a getter at N) passes: ownKeys returns N+1 keys (indices plus 'length' when no sparse getter is defined, or the out-of-range key when present). The type guard then returns true while silently ignoring an own key that the loop never inspects. It also returns true for a sparse hole whose index is absent only if the array length matches. The accessor is not executed (good), but a persisted payload with extra own properties is accepted as valid, so a strict later validator that relies on this guard could treat a padded record as clean.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted trace. Build targets = ['index.html'] and define a getter at property '1' on it (after setting length = 1). Reflect.ownKeys(targets) yields ['0','length','1'] → length 3, and targets.length+1 = 2, so line 18 returns false. However, define the getter at the symbol key or at a non-index key such as 'extra' while length is 1: ownKeys yields ['0','length','extra'] → 3 ≠ 2, so that path rejects. The remaining accepted hole is an array whose extra key replaces a missing index. The test at lines 114-115 covers only an index getter. The guard should assert every own key is a canonical index.
findings.suggestion: Validate own keys strictly: every own key must be either 'length' or a canonical index string less than length, and each index must have a data descriptor (no sparse holes). Reject otherwise. Add the non-index-extra-key and hole cases to the 108-116 test.

findings.title: Working-time-unit normalization applies before analysis, so 'hours of operation' text can be classified without the runtime obligation
findings.evidence: withoutWorkingTimeUnits is applied at line 172 (source-no-directive path), line 177 and line 179 to strip time units from 'working hours' phrasing. Its stated purpose is to keep business-hour copy source-checkable. That is correct for static opening-hour copy. The proposed obligation design, however, needs finite per-operation spans because the same words ('hours', 'open', 'accept bookings') can express a runtime booking capability. The normalizer runs before the FINANCIAL/RECORD/EMAIL vetoes at lines 168-170, and any phrase such as 'bookings open 24 hours' loses the time token before classification. This is a bounded normalization that can mask a runtime phrase. It is acceptable given the bounded allowlists, but it needs a pinned counterexample.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted trace. source='Reservations must be open for bookings 24 hours.' with no source-only directive: OBSERVATION_REQUIRED matches 'reservations?', so runtime_or_subjective is still returned. A source whose only runtime signal is the time unit, however, would skip the observation branch after normalization and fall to the manual/coverage unclassified branch. The test file has no such case.
findings.suggestion: Apply the operation vetoes (FINANCIAL/CARD/EMAIL/RECORD) to the raw combined text before normalization, and add a test where the only runtime cue is a time unit (for example 'open for bookings 24 hours') to pin the expected reason.

limitations: Read-only source-only review. No files were modified, no shell, test, typecheck, browser, model, or payment execution was performed. Every reproduction is an unexecuted static trace, and behavior in runtime (network, storage, UI) was not verified.

Only the five packet files were reviewed: lib/contracts.ts, lib/assessment-evidence-scope.ts, lib/assessment-evidence-needs.ts, tests/assessment-evidence-needs.test.ts, and the project skill. Imports not in the packet (exact-copy-directive, source-literal-directive, static-markup-directive, static-resources, delivery-assessment.ts, assessment-citation-catalog.ts, requirement-coverage.ts) were not inspected. The claimed server-side construction of evidence needs and the root integration (final items, UI, export, no parent promotion) are therefore unverified.

The cycle-20 proposal (deriveAssessmentObligations, activeV3, source-obligations-v1, up to 12 children, strict re-derivation validator across current and history, bilingual collapsed child statuses) is not in the packet. Findings on missing contract support and test gaps judge feasibility and risks of that design against the supplied types. They do not assert that the feature exists or is broken.

Award comparison (PHAROS_INC at the IBM Bob 2026 event, AgentReceipt at that event, and Jayu at Gemini 2024) was used only from the packet's summary; the external URLs were not fetched, and opponent internals were not audited. No claim of superiority or score comparison is made.
No runtime check of the official bemyapp winners page (dated after this review's static reading) or of the Google announcement was performed. The strengths cited are the official description only.
Negation handling in the regexes was not exhaustively enumerated: matches that appear only in adversarial prose depend on code not in the packet (delivery-assessment.ts).
No security findings are claimed. The scope of this review is correctness and product-flow, as requested.
